title: Was the Moon Landing Faked

lines.speaker: vale
lines.text: In July nineteen sixty nine, around six hundred million people watched Neil Armstrong step onto the Moon. Yet a stubborn minority insist it never happened at all.
lines.broll: The blue Earth rising over the grey cratered lunar horizon against a pitch black sky.

lines.speaker: vale
lines.text: So today, let's do something slightly unusual for a conspiracy channel. Let's take the hoax claims seriously, one by one, and test them against the evidence.
lines.broll: A dim study desk covered with old black and white space mission photographs, a brass magnifying glass and handwritten notes, warm lamp light.

lines.speaker: vale
lines.text: The idea really took off in nineteen seventy six, when a former rocket company writer, Bill Kaysing, self-published a book claiming the landings were staged.
lines.broll: A 1970s typewriter beside a tall stack of manuscript pages in a cluttered room, warm lamp light, no people.

lines.speaker: vale
lines.text: Claim one: the flag appears to wave, and there's no wind on the Moon. True, there's no wind, which is exactly why the flag behaves so strangely.
lines.broll: An American flag on a metal pole planted in grey lunar dust, held out by a horizontal rod along its top edge, harsh sunlight, black sky.

lines.speaker: vale
lines.text: It hung from a horizontal rod, and it only moved while the astronauts twisted the pole. With no air to slow it, the fabric kept swinging.
lines.broll: A close view of creased flag fabric hanging from a horizontal metal rod above grey lunar soil, harsh sunlight, black sky.

lines.speaker: vale
lines.text: Claim two: there are no stars in the photographs. But the lunar surface was in bright sunlight, and the cameras were set for daylight exposures.
lines.broll: A vintage silver medium format camera resting on grey lunar soil in harsh sunlight, a pitch black sky with no stars.

lines.speaker: vale
lines.text: Try photographing a starry sky from a floodlit stadium and you'll get the same result. The faint stars simply vanish against the glare.
lines.broll: An empty floodlit sports stadium at night, blazing lights, a black sky with no visible stars.

lines.speaker: vale
lines.text: Claim three: the shadows point in different directions, so there must be studio lights. In fact, uneven ground and wide angle lenses bend shadows naturally.
lines.broll: Rocks scattered across uneven cratered lunar ground casting long dark shadows at slightly different angles, low sun, black sky.

lines.speaker: vale
lines.text: Claim four: the Van Allen radiation belts would have killed the crew. The spacecraft crossed them in a few hours, on a path through their thinner regions.
lines.broll: A glowing band of faint blue-green radiation arcing around the Earth seen from deep space, a tiny distant spacecraft silhouette.

lines.speaker: vale
lines.text: And here's what the hoax theory can't explain. Apollo brought back three hundred and eighty two kilograms of Moon rock, studied by scientists around the world.
lines.broll: A grey lunar rock sample inside a sealed glass laboratory cabinet, clean white lab lighting, no people.

lines.speaker: vale
lines.text: Astronauts also left mirrors on the surface. Observatories still bounce lasers off them today, measuring the distance to the Moon to within millimetres.
lines.broll: A thin green laser beam shooting from an observatory dome into a night sky towards a bright full Moon.

lines.speaker: vale
lines.text: In two thousand nine, NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter photographed the landing sites from orbit, showing the descent stages and even the astronauts' footpaths.
lines.broll: A high overhead view of a grey lunar plain with a small lander base and faint dark footpath tracks leading away from it.

lines.speaker: vale
lines.text: Perhaps most telling of all, the Soviet Union was tracking every mission. Locked in a space race, they had every reason to cry foul, and never did.
lines.broll: A 1960s radar tracking station with a huge dish antenna at dusk under a cold sky, no people.

lines.speaker: vale
lines.text: So, was it faked? Every claim has an answer, and the evidence is still up there. Sometimes the official story really is the true one.
lines.broll: A full Moon rising slowly over a dark city skyline at night.
